questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What position is the patient in for Subcostal imaging?
options: Right lateral decubitus with the right arm raised above and resting under the head
Left lateral decubitus with the left arm raised above and resting under the head
questions.explanation: Subcostal imaging uses a supine position with the knees bent, which relaxes the abdominal wall and lets the transducer angle up under the costal margin toward the heart. *(Practice review slide 3.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  Where is the probe placed for the subcostal window?
options: Mid-chest on the patient’s left side at the 2nd–4th intercostal space
At the suprasternal notch with the indicator pointing toward 1–2 o’clock
At the level of the 5th or 6th intercostal space, mid-axillary line
Midline on the patient, located inferior to the xiphoid process
questions.explanation: The subcostal probe is placed in the midline just inferior to the xiphoid process, then angled up toward the left shoulder and heart. *(Practice review slide 5.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  The same anatomy will be demonstrated in the apical 4-chamber compared to the subcostal 4-chamber. Which answer is most accurate?
options: Cannot be determined from the image alone
questions.explanation: True — the subcostal 4-chamber displays the same four chambers, valves, and septa as the apical 4-chamber, just acquired from an inferior window with a different beam orientation. *(Practice review slide 7.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the right atrial pressure if the IVC is ≤2.1 cm and collapses more than 50%?
questions.explanation: An IVC ≤2.1 cm that collapses >50% with a sniff indicates a normal RA pressure, estimated at 3 mmHg (range 0–5). *(Practice review slide 9.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the right atrial pressure if the IVC is ≤2.1 cm and collapses less than 50%?
questions.explanation: A small IVC (≤2.1 cm) that collapses <50% is a discordant pattern, giving the intermediate RA pressure estimate of 8 mmHg (range 5–10). *(Practice review slide 11.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  What is the right atrial pressure if the IVC is ≥2.1 cm and collapses less than 50%?
questions.explanation: A dilated IVC (≥2.1 cm) that collapses <50% indicates a high RA pressure, estimated at 15 mmHg (range 10–20). *(Practice review slide 13.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From the subcostal 4-chamber, how do you maneuver the probe to acquire the subcostal short axis showing the long axis of the IVC?
options: Rotate the probe clockwise ~90° to place the indicator at 6 o’clock
Rotate the probe counterclockwise ~90° to place the indicator at 12 o’clock
Angle the probe toward the patient’s left shoulder
Angle the probe toward the patient’s right hip
questions.explanation: From the subcostal 4-chamber, rotate the probe counterclockwise ~90° (indicator toward 12 o’clock) to obtain the sagittal plane that shows the IVC in long axis entering the right atrium. *(Practice review slide 15.)*

questions.stem: During a routine adult transthoracic examination, the sonographer reviews the following concept.  From the subcostal short axis showing the long axis of the IVC, how do you maneuver the probe to acquire the descending aorta?
options: Rotate the probe clockwise until the descending aorta is in view
Rotate the probe counterclockwise until the descending aorta is in view
Angle and slide slightly left ward
questions.explanation: The course review identifies Angle and slide slightly left ward as the correct response. *(Practice review slide 17.)*
